Domain Description: Crop and livestock production, including day-to-day farm planning and operations before post-production distribution.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: On-farm crop and livestock production; excludes food logistics (D09), fisheries production (D10), and environmental measurement as the primary purpose (D18).
Why Explore This Domain?: A major local livelihood with observable production, coordination, and record-keeping processes.
Possible Context / Setting: Crop and livestock farms, cooperatives, agriculture offices, agribusinesses
Potential Stakeholders: Farmers, farm workers, cooperatives, agriculture officers, agribusiness operators
Processes Worth Exploring: Production planning, crop and livestock monitoring, irrigation, input use, disease reporting, harvest records, farm records
Access Basis / Contact Status: Possible route through agriculture offices or cooperatives; no named partner or farmer participation confirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: PSA and Department of Agriculture background data support sector relevance; exact Iloilo source citations and local process evidence are still required.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Farmer or cooperative access; incomplete farm records; seasonal crop cycles; field travel; connectivity and device constraints.
External Support / Facility Needs: Agriculture officer or cooperative partner; field instruments only if required by the selected process.
Next Validation Action: Secure one farm, cooperative, or agriculture-office partner and investigate one production process.

Domain Description: Educational processes directly related to instruction, assessment, academic records, and school administration.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Teaching, learning, assessment, academic records, and administration; excludes accessibility (D14), student support (D15), work transition (D16), and local-language resources (D22) as primary concerns.
Why Explore This Domain?: Students and educators are accessible, and many academic processes can be observed without assuming a technology.
Possible Context / Setting: Public and private schools, universities, classrooms, academic offices, learning environments
Potential Stakeholders: Students, teachers, academic coordinators, registrars, school administrators
Processes Worth Exploring: Instruction and learning-resource access, assessment, scheduling, enrollment, academic records, administrative workflows
Access Basis / Contact Status: Students are directly reachable; school staff, institutional approval, and authorized records remain unconfirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: DepEd policy and education statistics provide background; local school-process evidence and authorized records are not yet collected.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: School approval; student privacy; timetable constraints; uneven facilities and connectivity; access to authorized process records.
External Support / Facility Needs: School approval and cooperation from the relevant teacher, registrar, administrator, or student-service office.
Next Validation Action: Choose one school or campus process and obtain the required approval before collecting baseline evidence.

Application Domain: Healthcare Service Delivery and Public Health Operations
Domain Description: Delivery and coordination of clinical, community, and administrative health services, without assuming access to clinical data.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Formal healthcare and public-health service workflows; excludes routine public safety (D13) and non-clinical student support (D15) as primary concerns.
Why Explore This Domain?: The domain contains consequential service problems, but meaningful study requires a formal health-sector access pathway.
Possible Context / Setting: Rural health units, clinics, hospitals, public-health offices, community health programs
Potential Stakeholders: Patients, healthcare workers, health administrators, public-health personnel
Processes Worth Exploring: Appointments, queues, referrals, non-clinical records, service coordination, supply workflows, public-health reporting
Access Basis / Contact Status: No health-facility partner or approved access route has been confirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: DOH and WVMC public information provide background; no accessible local workflow records are confirmed.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Formal health-facility partner; ethics and privacy approval; restricted clinical records; professional oversight; limited testing access.
External Support / Facility Needs: Health-facility partner, ethics/privacy approval, and professional oversight.
Next Validation Action: Seek a non-clinical health-workflow partner and an ethics/privacy route; otherwise keep the domain deferred.

Application Domain: Passenger Mobility and Local Transport Operations
Domain Description: Movement of passengers through local transport services and the operations that support commuting and mobility.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Passenger mobility and transport operations; excludes food freight and logistics (D09) and destination-service management (D11).
Why Explore This Domain?: Commuter experiences and route conditions can be observed directly, while operational records may require permission.
Possible Context / Setting: Public-transport routes, terminals, urban corridors, campuses, parking areas
Potential Stakeholders: Students, commuters, drivers, operators, transport and traffic personnel
Processes Worth Exploring: Route use, waiting time, scheduling, passenger information, terminal operations, parking, mobility accessibility
Access Basis / Contact Status: Commuters are directly reachable and routes are observable; TTMO, drivers, and operators remain unconfirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: Direct route observations and commuter interviews are feasible; TTMO or operator records are unverified.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: TTMO or route-operator permission; route and traffic records may be unavailable; time and seasonal variation; field-observation safety.
External Support / Facility Needs: TTMO or route/operator cooperation if operational records are required.
Next Validation Action: Conduct timed observations and commuter interviews on one route, then determine whether agency records are necessary.

Domain Description: Hazard-specific planning and coordinated action that reduce risk and prepare communities before and during emergencies.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Hazard-risk reduction and preparedness; excludes routine safety response (D13), environmental measurement (D18), and long-term adaptation planning (D19).
Why Explore This Domain?: Communities face recurring hazards, and preparedness processes can be examined before selecting a technology.
Possible Context / Setting: Hazard-prone barangays, evacuation centers, schools, municipal DRRM operations
Potential Stakeholders: Residents, barangay officials, DRRMO personnel, responders, school safety staff
Processes Worth Exploring: Risk communication, preparedness planning, warning dissemination, evacuation planning, drills, relief readiness
Access Basis / Contact Status: Residents may be reachable; barangay or DRRMO participation and operational records require approval.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: PDRRMO/CDRRMO plans and public hazard information provide background; local process evidence is not yet collected.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: PDRRMO or LGU permission; sensitive incident records; responder availability; emergency testing limits; hazard-specific scope.
External Support / Facility Needs: Barangay or LGU DRRMO partner and a safe drill, simulation, or planning setting.
Next Validation Action: Select one hazard, locality, and preparedness process, then contact the relevant barangay or DRRMO.

Domain Description: Management of water supply, distribution, use, routine quality oversight, and related service infrastructure.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Water supply, distribution, use, and service operations; excludes environmental measurement as the primary purpose (D18) and ecosystem-restoration management (D25).
Why Explore This Domain?: Water-service conditions affect households and institutions and contain observable reporting and operational processes.
Possible Context / Setting: Communities, campuses, farms, water districts, shared water systems
Potential Stakeholders: Households, water providers, barangay officials, farmers, facility managers
Processes Worth Exploring: Supply scheduling, usage records, leak reporting, routine quality checks, pump and storage operations, service complaints
Access Basis / Contact Status: Households may be reachable; water-provider, district, and laboratory access remain unconfirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: Water-agency and EMB sources provide background; provider records and water-quality evidence are unverified.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Utility or provider permission; restricted operational data; sampling and laboratory costs; seasonal variation; data ownership.
External Support / Facility Needs: Water provider; calibrated instruments and a reference laboratory if water-quality testing is selected.
Next Validation Action: Choose supply, quality, conservation, or irrigation, then secure the matching provider and evidence route.

Domain Description: Operational processes for segregating, collecting, recovering, recycling, treating, and disposing of solid waste.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Solid-waste operations; excludes environmental-condition measurement (D18) and ecosystem-restoration management (D25).
Why Explore This Domain?: Waste operations are visible in schools and communities and can produce measurable evidence at a bounded site.
Possible Context / Setting: Campuses, barangays, markets, collection points, materials recovery facilities
Potential Stakeholders: Households, students, facility staff, waste collectors, barangay and municipal personnel
Processes Worth Exploring: Segregation, collection scheduling, route operations, recovery and recycling, reporting, waste-volume recording
Access Basis / Contact Status: Campus or barangay observation is feasible; no approved site, MRF, or LGU partner is confirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: Official solid-waste policy and direct site audits can provide evidence; no local baseline or approved site is confirmed.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Barangay or campus permission; sanitation and PPE; consistent waste measurement; collector cooperation; behavior variability.
External Support / Facility Needs: Campus, barangay, or MRF approval; PPE and a consistent waste-measurement protocol.
Next Validation Action: Select one campus or barangay site, obtain permission, and conduct a baseline audit of one waste process.

Application Domain: Energy Use and Facility Energy Management
Domain Description: Operational monitoring and management of energy use, reliability, and efficiency in households and facilities.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Energy-use and facility-energy operations; excludes water-service operations (D06) and general residential maintenance (D17).
Why Explore This Domain?: Energy use creates measurable costs and service concerns in homes, schools, businesses, and public facilities.
Possible Context / Setting: Homes, campuses, offices, small businesses, public buildings
Potential Stakeholders: Households, students, facility managers, business owners, power-service personnel
Processes Worth Exploring: Consumption records, peak-use assessment, equipment scheduling, outage reporting, facility energy assessment
Access Basis / Contact Status: Household or campus access is plausible; facility and utility records require permission.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: DOE and distributor sources provide background; facility-level consumption and equipment records are unverified.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Meter or utility data access; electrical safety; hardware cost; facility permission; changing usage patterns.
External Support / Facility Needs: Facility manager, electrical-safety supervision, and meters or sensors if hardware is involved.
Next Validation Action: Choose one facility and one issue—consumption, reliability, scheduling, or reporting—and verify data and safety access.

Domain Description: Movement, handling, storage, and coordination of food after production through markets and consumers.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Post-production food movement, handling, storage, and coordination; excludes farm or fisheries production (D01, D10) and passenger transport (D04).
Why Explore This Domain?: Delays, spoilage, stock uncertainty, and coordination problems may be observable when one commodity chain is selected.
Possible Context / Setting: Farms and landing points, markets, cooperatives, storage areas, retailers, delivery routes
Potential Stakeholders: Producers, traders, vendors, transporters, retailers, consumers
Processes Worth Exploring: Inventory recording, storage conditions, shipment and delivery coordination, demand records, traceability, spoilage reporting
Access Basis / Contact Status: Vendors and consumers may be reachable; no commodity-chain partner or commercial records are confirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: Sector reports and participant interviews may provide evidence; commodity-specific commercial records are unverified.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Commercially sensitive records; fragmented supply-chain data; seasonal supply; cold-storage access; participant availability.
External Support / Facility Needs: One commodity-chain partner and storage or cold-chain access if relevant.
Next Validation Action: Reconsider only after one commodity-chain partner and one transition point are confirmed.

Domain Description: Capture fisheries and farmed aquatic production, including operational and biological processes before distribution.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Fisheries and aquaculture production; excludes post-production food logistics (D09) and general environmental monitoring (D18).
Why Explore This Domain?: The sector is locally important, but research requires sustained access to production sites, operators, or technical experts.
Possible Context / Setting: Fishing communities, fishponds, landing sites, hatcheries, aquaculture facilities
Potential Stakeholders: Fishers, fish farmers, fisheries officers, technical experts, coastal communities
Processes Worth Exploring: Production planning, feeding, stock and catch records, disease observation, harvest, landing records
Access Basis / Contact Status: No committed fisheries site, operator, expert, dataset, or laboratory access is confirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: BFAR, UPV, and SEAFDEC sources provide background; site datasets, expert labels, and laboratory access are unverified.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Sustained field-site and fisher access; BFAR, UPV, or SEAFDEC expert support; equipment and laboratory fees; weather and seasonality.
External Support / Facility Needs: BFAR, UPV, SEAFDEC, or equivalent expert support; field site and possible laboratory or equipment.
Next Validation Action: Reconsider only after a fisheries partner, field site, expert, schedule, and total cost are confirmed.

Domain Description: Visitor-facing services and the operation and management of tourism destinations, accommodations, and activities.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Visitor and destination services; excludes passenger transport as the primary process (D04) and cultural safeguarding (D20).
Why Explore This Domain?: Local destinations allow observation of visitor and operator processes, subject to site cooperation and seasonality.
Possible Context / Setting: Heritage and natural sites, festivals, tourism offices, accommodations, transport terminals
Potential Stakeholders: Visitors, residents, tourism officers, guides, transport providers, local businesses
Processes Worth Exploring: Visitor information, bookings and inquiries, visitor flow, accessibility, feedback, site and destination operations
Access Basis / Contact Status: Visitors may be reachable; tourism-office, site, and business cooperation remain unconfirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: DOT and local-tourism reports provide background; site-specific visitor and process evidence is unverified.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Tourism-site and business permission; seasonality; visitor recruitment; commercially sensitive records; heritage and community sensitivity.
External Support / Facility Needs: Tourism office, site manager, or participating business approval.
Next Validation Action: Select one destination and one visitor or operator process, then confirm site cooperation.

Application Domain: Government Service Delivery and Administrative Workflows
Domain Description: Citizen-facing transactions and internal administrative workflows of government offices, independent of sector-specific program content.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Citizen-facing government transactions and administrative workflows; excludes sector-specific problems merely because an LGU operates the service.
Why Explore This Domain?: Citizens regularly use public offices, allowing investigation of service access, delays, routing, and transparency.
Possible Context / Setting: Barangay halls, municipal offices, service counters, public consultations
Potential Stakeholders: Citizens, barangay officials, municipal staff, applicants, civil-society groups
Processes Worth Exploring: Applications, permits, document requests, complaints, case routing, public information, feedback, processing-time recording
Access Basis / Contact Status: Citizens are reachable; LGU staff participation and transaction records require authorization.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: DILG, ARTA, and Citizen's Charter documents provide process baselines; actual local transaction data are unverified.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: LGU permission; protected records; policy variation; staff workload; process ownership; Citizen's Charter may not reflect actual practice.
External Support / Facility Needs: LGU or barangay-office approval and authorized access to non-sensitive process records.
Next Validation Action: Select one government transaction and office, then map the current process with authorized participants.

Domain Description: Prevention, reporting, coordination, and response for routine community-safety incidents and emergencies not primarily focused on natural-hazard planning.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Routine safety-incident reporting and emergency response; excludes natural-hazard preparedness (D05) and long-term climate adaptation (D19).
Why Explore This Domain?: Safety reporting and response coordination are consequential but require careful handling of operational information.
Possible Context / Setting: Barangays, schools, public spaces, transport areas, emergency operations centers
Potential Stakeholders: Residents, barangay officials, responders, school safety staff, enforcement personnel
Processes Worth Exploring: Incident reporting, dispatch, public advisories, response coordination, resource status, after-action records
Access Basis / Contact Status: Community users may be reachable; responder participation and incident records require formal authorization.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: Public-safety policies and advisories provide background; incident and response records are restricted.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Sensitive incident and security data; agency permission; respondent safety; false or incomplete reports; no testing in real emergencies.
External Support / Facility Needs: Agency or responder partner and a controlled, non-emergency evaluation environment.
Next Validation Action: Retain one safe public-information or coordination process and obtain an agency partner.

Domain Description: Conditions and barriers affecting equitable access to digital services, communication, mobility, learning, and public participation.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Accessibility barriers and inclusive participation; excludes assuming assistive technology as the solution and excludes general education operations.
Parent / Related Domain IDs: Related: D02, D04, D11, D15, D22
Why Explore This Domain?: Accessibility becomes researchable when representative users help define needs and evaluation criteria.
Possible Context / Setting: Schools, campuses, homes, public facilities, websites, mobile services
Potential Stakeholders: People with disabilities, caregivers, educators, accessibility advocates, service providers
Processes Worth Exploring: Accessibility assessment, digital navigation, communication access, wayfinding, service accommodation, usability evaluation
Access Basis / Contact Status: PDAO, CSWDO, or advocacy routes are possible; representative participants and a qualified validator are unconfirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: Accessibility standards and participatory evidence are appropriate; representative local evidence has not been collected.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Representative participant recruitment; informed consent; diverse accessibility needs; assistive-device availability; expert validation.
External Support / Facility Needs: Representative users, an accessibility specialist, and appropriate assistive devices.
Next Validation Action: Secure representative participants and a qualified accessibility validator before defining requirements.

Application Domain: Student Support Services and Academic Well-being
Domain Description: Non-clinical academic, social, and support-service conditions affecting students' participation and ability to learn.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Non-clinical student-support and academic-well-being processes; excludes health diagnosis or treatment (D03) and general teaching processes (D02).
Why Explore This Domain?: The group can access students and observe service-discovery, workload, and support-process concerns.
Possible Context / Setting: Universities, schools, classrooms, student-service offices, online learning environments
Potential Stakeholders: Students, teachers, guidance personnel, student-affairs staff, parents or guardians when appropriate
Processes Worth Exploring: Workload coordination, support-service discovery, appointments, campus participation, referrals, follow-up
Access Basis / Contact Status: Students are reachable; student-service staff participation and sensitive records require institutional approval.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: Student interviews, observation, and public service information may provide evidence; sensitive institutional records are restricted.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Sensitive personal data; school ethics or approval; measurement validity; professional oversight; avoid collecting clinical disclosures.
External Support / Facility Needs: School ethics/approval and guidance or student-services oversight.
Next Validation Action: Narrow to one non-clinical support-service process and obtain campus approval.

Domain Description: Preparation for work, skills development, recruitment, career guidance, and transition from education to employment.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Career preparation, skills, recruitment, and school-to-work transition; excludes general teaching (D02) and internal MSME operations (D23).
Why Explore This Domain?: Students, graduates, training providers, and employers may reveal measurable skills and transition mismatches.
Possible Context / Setting: Universities, training centers, job fairs, local firms, recruitment channels
Potential Stakeholders: Students, graduates, career offices, trainers, employers, local businesses
Processes Worth Exploring: Skills-requirement analysis, career guidance, job and internship matching, credential records, employer coordination
Access Basis / Contact Status: Students and graduates are reachable; employer, PESO, and career-office participation remain unconfirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: DOLE, PESO, TESDA, and labor-market sources support relevance; an occupation-specific local mismatch is not validated.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Employer and career-office participation; self-reported skills; changing job requirements; personal-data privacy; outcome follow-up.
External Support / Facility Needs: Employer, PESO, or career-office partner and authorized skills or outcome data.
Next Validation Action: Select one occupation or school-to-work transition and confirm employer or career-office participation.

Application Domain: Housing, Rental, and Shared Residential Services
Domain Description: Residential, rental, maintenance, and shared-facility processes affecting tenants, landlords, and communities.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Housing, rental, maintenance, and shared-residential processes; excludes utilities, waste, public safety, and governance when those are the primary problem.
Why Explore This Domain?: Boarding and community-living experiences may reveal observable service and coordination problems.
Possible Context / Setting: Rental housing, dormitories, subdivisions, barangays, shared residential facilities
Potential Stakeholders: Residents, tenants, landlords, homeowners, barangay officials, maintenance personnel
Processes Worth Exploring: Maintenance requests, rental communication, community notices, shared-facility scheduling, residential reporting
Access Basis / Contact Status: The team has direct boarding experience; landlord, manager, and maintenance-record access remain unconfirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: Direct observation and interviews in boarding or rental settings are feasible; standardized operational records may be limited.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Private-property and household access; tenant and landlord privacy; differing responsibilities; limited standardized records.
External Support / Facility Needs: Landlord or boarding-manager cooperation and tenant consent.
Next Validation Action: Choose one boarding or rental workflow and confirm both resident and responsible-party access.

Domain Description: Systematic observation and measurement of environmental conditions using defined variables, sites, and reference methods.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Validated observation and measurement of environmental conditions; excludes restoration-project management (D25) and utility-service operations (D06).
Parent / Related Domain IDs: Related: D06, D07, D10, D19, D25
Why Explore This Domain?: Local conditions can be measured, but a viable study requires a validated variable, reference method, and sampling plan.
Possible Context / Setting: Rivers, watersheds, farms, roadsides, campuses, vulnerable or protected areas
Potential Stakeholders: Residents, environmental officers, schools, farmers, community groups, technical experts
Processes Worth Exploring: Sampling, sensor and field observations, data-quality checks, reporting, trend analysis, threshold assessment
Access Basis / Contact Status: Potential field sites exist; site permission, expert validation, calibration, and laboratory access remain unconfirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: EMB, DOST VI, and UPV technical references provide pathways; the variable-specific dataset and reference method are unconfirmed.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Site permission; sensor calibration; reference laboratory or technical validation; sampling duration; weather exposure; maintenance cost.
External Support / Facility Needs: Environmental expert, calibrated sensors/reference instruments, and laboratory or technical validation.
Next Validation Action: Select one environmental variable, site, reference method, sampling period, and total validation cost.

Domain Description: Planning and prioritization of actions that help communities and systems adjust to projected climate impacts over longer time horizons.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Long-term climate planning and adaptation-option prioritization; excludes immediate disaster preparedness (D05) and environmental measurement (D18).
Why Explore This Domain?: The domain is relevant only when narrowed to a planning or resource-allocation decision distinct from preparedness and monitoring.
Possible Context / Setting: Coastal areas, flood-prone communities, agricultural zones, local planning offices
Potential Stakeholders: Local governments, vulnerable communities, environmental planners, researchers
Processes Worth Exploring: Vulnerability assessment, adaptation-option prioritization, local planning, project monitoring, resource allocation
Access Basis / Contact Status: Public climate data may be available; LGU planners, plans, and local raw data require confirmation.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: PAGASA and GeoRisk public data provide background; local adaptation-decision evidence is unverified.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Long-term data and evaluation horizon; model complexity; overlap with DRR and environmental monitoring; LGU planning access; policy dependence.
External Support / Facility Needs: LGU planning/environment office and climate-data expertise.
Next Validation Action: Choose one planning decision with a feasible historical, simulation, or expert-evaluation basis; otherwise drop.

Application Domain: Financial Access and Consumer Service Workflows
Domain Description: Access to, understanding of, and support for formal financial services, payments, microfinance, and financial-literacy services.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Consumer access to, understanding of, and support for financial services; excludes credit scoring and internal business management (D23).
Why Explore This Domain?: Local consumers and merchants may reveal barriers in service discovery, onboarding, understanding, and assistance.
Possible Context / Setting: Stores, cooperatives, rural banks, payment agents, schools, community financial-literacy programs
Potential Stakeholders: Consumers, small merchants, cooperative members, financial-literacy educators, financial-service personnel
Processes Worth Exploring: Financial-literacy support, service discovery, onboarding, payment assistance, complaint handling, consumer-side record reconciliation
Access Basis / Contact Status: Consumers and merchants may be reachable; financial-service providers and transaction records are restricted.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: BSP financial-inclusion and consumer-protection sources provide background; local workflow evidence is unverified.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Financial-data sensitivity; regulated services; trust and informed consent; transaction records unavailable; avoid collecting credentials or balances.
External Support / Facility Needs: Consumer-protection or financial-literacy expert; no credentials, balances, or transaction access.
Next Validation Action: Choose one non-sensitive consumer workflow and define an ethical participant/evidence plan.

Domain Description: Day-to-day processes used by micro and small enterprises to manage sales, products, suppliers, customers, and digital channels.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Internal MSME sales, inventory, supplier, customer, and digital-commerce operations; excludes consumer financial access (D21) and whole food-supply chains (D09).
Why Explore This Domain?: Local enterprises provide observable manual and digital workflows without requiring a predetermined solution.
Possible Context / Setting: Stores, market stalls, home-based enterprises, cooperatives, small online shops
Potential Stakeholders: Small-business owners, market vendors, home-based sellers, customers, suppliers, business-support personnel
Processes Worth Exploring: Inventory and stock records, supplier ordering, sales recording, payment reconciliation, customer inquiries, business reporting
Access Basis / Contact Status: Local business owners are reachable in principle; no committed business partner or record access is confirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: DTI and PSA MSME sources support relevance; partner business records and a local bottleneck remain unconfirmed.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Owner availability; inconsistent records; commercial privacy; device and connectivity constraints; avoid sensitive financial or customer data.
External Support / Facility Needs: Committed MSME partner and access to non-sensitive operational records.
Next Validation Action: Choose one business type and committed partner, then quantify one recurring non-sensitive operational bottleneck.

Application Domain: Digital Safety and Data Privacy Practices
Domain Description: Safe, lawful, and responsible handling of personal data, accounts, devices, and online interactions when security or privacy is the primary research concern.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Security or privacy must be the primary research problem; excludes treating it only as a requirement of another domain. All studies must be controlled and authorized.
Why Explore This Domain?: Local practices and support workflows can be examined safely through controlled and authorized studies.
Possible Context / Setting: Schools, campuses, public offices, local businesses, community organizations, online groups
Potential Stakeholders: Students, educators, parents or guardians, office staff, business owners, data-protection personnel
Processes Worth Exploring: Privacy-notice comprehension, consent, account-security practices, scam recognition and reporting, incident reporting, permissions, data retention
Access Basis / Contact Status: Students and MSMEs are reachable for controlled studies; organizational systems and incident logs remain restricted.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: NPC, DICT, and CICC materials provide background; a specific local user or workflow problem is not yet validated.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Participant privacy and informed consent; access to incident logs is restricted; institutional authorization; controlled testing only; no unauthorized access.
External Support / Facility Needs: Institutional authorization and a controlled cybersecurity/privacy study environment.
Next Validation Action: Choose one controlled awareness, usability, reporting, or privacy workflow and obtain institutional authorization.

Application Domain: Cultural Heritage Documentation and Knowledge Transmission
Domain Description: Documentation, safeguarding, and community-controlled transmission of local traditions, oral histories, languages, and cultural knowledge.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Safeguarding and transmitting cultural knowledge with community permission; excludes tourism services (D11) and language-literacy resources (D22) as the primary purpose.
Why Explore This Domain?: Local documentation and knowledge-transmission practices may contain access, continuity, ownership, and validation concerns that can be investigated with community permission.
Possible Context / Setting: One consenting barangay, cultural organization, local heritage office, or school-based local-history setting in Iloilo or Antique
Potential Stakeholders: Cultural knowledge holders, community elders, local historians, cultural organizations, barangay or cultural offices, educators, and learners
Processes Worth Exploring: Existing documentation, consent and ownership practices, transcription, cataloging, access control, community validation, and knowledge transmission
Access Basis / Contact Status: No specific community, cultural office, gatekeeper, or knowledge-holder permission is confirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: NCCA cultural-inventory and heritage-documentation programs provide background; local community evidence is not yet obtained.
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Requires trust-building and consent from elders/communities; cultural sensitivity in handling and presenting oral knowledge; access to community gatekeepers (e.g., barangay or cultural office) is essential before any data collection; risk of misrepresentation if not community-validated.
External Support / Facility Needs: Community gatekeeper, cultural knowledge holders, and NCCA or local-cultural-office guidance.
Next Validation Action: Select one consenting community and cultural practice, obtain permission, and confirm the revised scope with the submitter.

Domain Description: Reading, writing, translation, comprehension, and preservation of Hiligaynon, Kinaray-a, and other regional-language resources.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Local-language literacy and resource processes; excludes general academic administration (D02) and cultural documentation not centered on language or literacy (D20).
Why Explore This Domain?: Changes under RA 12027 make local-language resource availability, classroom use, and literacy support worth exploring, but a specific local difficulty must be verified with educators and learners.
Possible Context / Setting: Schools, community literacy programs, libraries, cultural organizations, and local-language resource projects
Potential Stakeholders: Students, teachers, local-language advocates or linguists, librarians, DepEd personnel
Processes Worth Exploring: Language mapping, local-language resource cataloging, reading support, transcription, translation assistance, and material evaluation
Access Basis / Contact Status: Students and teachers may be reachable; no educator, linguist, or validated language-resource partner is confirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: RA 12027 and education/language-resource sources provide policy background; a local literacy or resource problem is not yet validated. https://lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2024/ra_12027_2024.html
Initial Concerns / Constraints: Policy alignment under RA 12027, limited validated datasets, orthography and linguistic expertise, and permissions for copyrighted or community materials
External Support / Facility Needs: Educator or linguist, KWF/DepEd-aligned resources, and copyright or community permissions.
Next Validation Action: Choose one language/literacy process and local setting, then confirm an educator or linguist and submitter approval.

Domain Description: Planning, coordination, documentation, and management of mangrove restoration activities and their project-level outcomes.
Scope Boundary / Exclusions: Mangrove-restoration planning, coordination, field records, and project reporting; excludes scientific environmental-condition measurement as the primary purpose (D18) and generic waste or water-service operations.
Parent / Related Domain IDs: Related: D06, D07, D10, D18, D19
Why Explore This Domain?: Mangrove-restoration projects involve field records, activity coordination, survival tracking, and reporting processes that may warrant investigation when one site and responsible organization are accessible.
Possible Context / Setting: One verified mangrove-restoration site in Iloilo; Leganes Integrated Katunggan Ecopark is a documented candidate, but research access is unconfirmed
Potential Stakeholders: Site managers, LGU environment offices, DENR or BFAR personnel, fisherfolk, conservation organizations, community partners, volunteers, and researchers
Processes Worth Exploring: Restoration planning, planting-site records, project-level survival and growth tracking, field-data collection, activity and volunteer coordination, reporting, and decision-making
Access Basis / Contact Status: The submitter has a personal contact connected to relevant mangrove-restoration stakeholders. The organization or role, possible type of access, willingness to participate, authority, and required permissions remain to be confirmed.
Preliminary Evidence / Source Basis: Official documentation confirms mangrove-restoration activity at Leganes Integrated Katunggan Ecopark.
